Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public. 




Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan 
"The Right to Information, The Right to Live"

1. Scope — Dimensions and other requirements for medicine ball, used for physical training. 

2. Material 

2.1 Outer CoverjCase — Shoulder portion (minimum thickness 2 mm) of tight textured cow-hide 
leather, free from flay cuts and grain defects, vegetable tanned, semi-chrome tanned or chrome 
tanned, natural or dyed in any colour as agreed to between the purchaser and the manufacturer. 
However, at the end of tanning operation and before drying, suitable fungicides shall be Incorporated 
into the leather and these shall be effective and non-toxic. Further the tanned leather shall 
be substantially fat-liquored and grain finished smooth. The panels of leather used for construction 
shall be such as will stretch uniformally, so as to avoid the ball losing shape in usage. 

2.2 Backing 

a) Cotton dosuti [see IS : 179-1965 Specification for dosuti (revised)], 

b) Unbleached linen, made from pure long lone flax, complying with the following particulars: 

i) Weight per square metre = 246'5 g 
ii) Threads per dcm ( approx ) = 220 ( Warp ), 



190 ( Weft ) 



2.3 Thread for Stitching 



a) Lightly waxed flax thread, having minimum breaking strength of 28 kgf on 50 cm gauge 
length. 

b) 60 tex x 3 (or 10 s/3) cotton thread, having a single thread minimum breaking load of 
4'10 kgf on 50 cm gauge length ( see IS : 1720-1969 Specification for cotton sewing thread, 
bleached or dyed). 

2.4 Pack 

a) New linear jute padding 



b) Long fibre Indian kapok (see IS: 3040-1965 
Specification for Indian kapok for stuffing 
purposes) 

c) Linen padding, and 

d) Compressed rubber pieces. 

3. Dimensions and Weight — Shall be as follows: 



Soft, smooth, clean, dry, reasonably free 
from extraneous matter and silky in 
appearance

IS: 8594 -1977 

4. Manufacture — The ball shall consist of a leather outer case with the leather assembled flesh 
side outwards or grain side outwards, as agreed to between the purchaser and the manufacturer. 
The inside shall be tightly packed with linen, jute or kapok padding or any other suitable material 
approved by the purchaser. ( In case of Defence supplies, prior to padding the material shall be 
bound with dosuti and sewing cotton thread into a spherical shape). The case shall comprise 
eight panels and two caps, which shall be strongly sewn in conjunction with the panels and the 
linen backing if the leather is backed, using a lightly waxed flax thread or cotton thread 
if so required by the purchaser. The stitching shall be spaced 25 to 28 stitches per decimetre. ( In 
case of Defence supplies, the case shall comprise two identical panels, suitably blocked and laced 
together by means of leather laces, 4'8 mm in width and 2 mm in substance, with edges tappered 
throughout. The lacing holes shall be punched 12 mm apart and 6 mm from the edge of each 
panel ). 

s a Workmanship and Finish — The balls shall be spherical in shape and have a neat finish, 

6. Marking — Each ball shall be clearly and indelibly marked with the manufacturer's name, initials 
or registered trade-mark and its weight. 

6*1 ISI Certification Marking — Details available with the Indian Standards Institution, 

7. Packing — As required by the purchaser. 



Printed at Neelkamal Printers, Delhi, India
